newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BAILEY MAKES SLUGGISH START TO WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY MAKES SLUGGISH START TO WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Canadian Donovan Bailey made a sluggish start in his defence of his 100 metres title at the world championship on Saturday, finishing second in his first round heat.

Bailey, the world record holder and Olympic champion who has yet to strike top form this season, was last out of the blocks, trailed the field at the 25 metre mark, and accelerated quickly through the middle of the race to take his place in the second round.
While his qualification never looked in doubt, it was not a performance that would have struck fear into the hearts of his major rivals.
But they all know Bailey improves dramatically through the rounds at a major championship and is likely to perform far better in the second round later on Saturday.
The fans in the stadium were not all that bothered about his performances, especially as he finished behind Agelos Pavlakakis of Greece who won in 10.11 seconds. Bailey clocked 10.17.

Ato Boldon of Trinidad, a strong contender for both the 100 and 200 titles, also clocked 10.11 to win his heat, while American champion Maurice Greene, another gold medal prospect cruised home in 10.32 to win his race.
"I felt good" said the Trinidadian, "I'm just focusing on the final. The time is fine for the first round but you're going to have to be real fast to win the gold."
